title: Centralize Automation and CI/CD
objective: Explain how automation controllers and CI systems run governed Ansible jobs.

sourceAlignment.title: Ansible for DevOps, 2nd Edition
sourceAlignment.author: Jeff Geerling
sourceAlignment.chapterTitle: Automating Your Automation with Ansible Tower and CI/CD
sourceAlignment.note: Original companion material. Uses the current generic term automation controller while retaining the book's AWX/Tower context.

paragraphs: AWX and commercial automation controllers add a web interface, API, schedules, credentials, inventories, job templates, logs, notifications, and role-based access around ansible-playbook.
A job template binds a project revision, inventory, credentials, playbook, and launch policy. Centralized credentials should be injected at runtime and access should follow least privilege.

CI tools such as Jenkins can lint, test, and launch playbooks after changes. The same pattern applies across modern CI platforms: version control triggers a repeatable pipeline and preserves auditable results.
explanation.rule: Keep automation in version control; let controllers supply governed execution, credentials, and audit history.

examples.title: Job Template Model
examples.code:
job_template:
  project: infrastructure
  inventory: staging
  playbook: site.yml
  ask_limit_on_launch: true
examples.note: This is a conceptual configuration artifact, not an exported AWX schema.

checks.question: What does an automation controller add around playbooks?
options: Governed execution, credentials, scheduling, and audit history

feedback.incorrect: Controllers operationalize playbooks; they do not replace their source.

assignment.title: Define a Safe Job Template
assignment.brief: Model a staging site.yml job that asks for a host limit at launch.
requirements: Set project, inventory, playbook, and ask_limit_on_launch.
assignment.solutionCode:

  project: infrastructure
  inventory: staging
  playbook: site.yml
  ask_limit_on_launch: true
